name: $47 branding vs. $5,000 branding
object: Softriver's full brand-identity package, shown against a cheap generic logo as the point of contrast
audience: founders comparing a cheap logo gig to a real branding agency before they spend
message: This video tells founders shopping for a logo that a $47 mark looks shiny for a second, but a $5,000 Softriver brand system is the only one built with the strategy and assets to actually work everywhere.

moments.what: The creative director sits close to camera in a softly lit office and holds up a card reading the price contrast, setting the comparison he's about to make.
A $47 label appears over a generic gold-on-black 'Mystify' logo mockup collage: building signage, a phone app icon, a business card. It looks fine at a glance but generic.

A $5000 label cuts to the real brand system: a typography spec sheet (Helvetica Neue in several weights), a brand-imagery mood board, and a business-card and stationery layout, each held a beat so the craft is visible.
moments.copy: $5000 — primary typeface, brand imagery, brand stationery

moments.what: The sequence closes on the finished stationery shot while he poses the rhetorical question that doubles as the pitch, pushing viewers toward the bio link.
moments.copy: So what do you think you're actually paying for?

cta: No on-screen button — the close is a rhetorical question ('what are you really paying for?') paired with the caption's 'visit softriver.co / DM to get started', so the proof itself is the pitch.
why: The before/after price tag is instant and needs no narration to parse: one glance at the generic $47 mark next to the full $5,000 system (typography, imagery, stationery) tells the story. Ending on the rhetorical question rather than a hard sell lets the comparison do the persuading, which suits a scroll-stopping reel under 15 seconds.
